guideTitle: Best Rice Cookers for Sticky Rice (2026)
metaTitle: Best Rice Cookers for Sticky Rice (2026)
metaDescription: Seven rice cookers compared for sticky and glutinous rice: soak time, water ratio, steaming trays, fuzzy logic and the capacity that suits your household.
expertTake: The Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 is the best rice cooker for sticky rice because its neuro fuzzy logic and menu selections adjust heat to the grain. The CUCKOO CR-0375FG is the value pick with an explicit glutinous rice mode in a small body. Anyone who makes sticky rice for a crowd should skip small units and buy a bigger cooker or a bamboo steamer, since a single batch is the limit of every machine here.
introParagraphs: Sticky or glutinous rice behaves differently from ordinary rice. It has almost no free starch structure that holds grains apart, so it needs less water and benefits from a long soak. Traditional cooks steam it over boiling water, which is why many rice cookers make decent sticky rice only when used carefully.

This guide compares seven cookers for that job, looking at menu options, steam trays, heating control and capacity. We rely on the listing specs and general knowledge of how short-grain and glutinous rice cook. The key questions are how much water you can control, whether the cooker has a sweet or glutinous setting and how easy cleanup is after a very sticky batch.

products.name: Zojirushi NS-ZCC10 Neuro Fuzzy Rice Cooker and Warmer 5.5 Cup
products.description:
The NS-ZCC10 is a computerized cooker with neuro fuzzy logic that adjusts heating through the cycle. The spherical nonstick inner pan promotes uniform heating, and the cooker offers multiple menu selections, automatic and extended keep-warm, and reheat cycles. For glutinous rice, that control matters because sticky rice scorches easily and needs steady, gentle heat.

The tradeoff is cost and capacity. It is among the most expensive models here, and 5.5 cups uncooked is enough for a family, not a gathering. It is also a rice cooker, so it does not steam a bamboo basket the way traditional sticky rice is made, and you must handle soaking and water yourself.

Ownership is easy: wash the inner pan, inner lid and steam vent, and wipe the heating plate. A retractable cord and wall mount help storage. Compared with a basic cooker, it holds a more even temperature and is far less likely to leave a burned layer. Its retractable cord and wall-mount option also make it easy to store when it is not in use.
products.bestFor: Cooks who make sticky rice often and want consistent control.
pros: Neuro fuzzy logic adjusts heat through the cycle
cons: Costs far more than basic cookers
Does not replace a traditional steamer

products.name: CUCKOO CR-0375FG Micom Fuzzy Logic Rice Cooker 3 Cup
products.description:
The CUCKOO CR-0375FG is a small Korean cooker with fuzzy logic and menus that the listing says run from glutinous white rice to other grains. A dedicated glutinous option sets the water, soak and heat for you, which removes the biggest source of failure with sticky rice. It also has a self-clean function that helps with starchy residue.

Its compromise is size. Three cups uncooked yields six cups cooked, enough for two to four people but not for a family dinner or a gathering. Compared with the Zojirushi it has less advanced control and a smaller pot, but it costs less.

Keep the lid and steam vent clean because sticky rice leaves a thick residue. Use the paddle on the nonstick pot and wash it promptly. It is a smart pick for small households that want a purpose-built sticky rice setting. Its small footprint also means it fits comfortably next to a kettle without taking over a counter.
products.bestFor: Small households that want a dedicated glutinous rice mode.
cons: 3 cups uncooked is small for families
Nonstick pot needs a soft paddle

products.badge: Best for Rice and a Side Dish
products.name: Tiger JBV-A10U 5.5 Cup Micom Rice Cooker with Tacook Tray

specList.label: Feature
specList.value: Cooks rice and a dish together

products.description:
The Tiger JBV-A10U is a microcomputer controlled cooker with a tacook tray that lets you cook a main dish above the rice at the same time. The listing describes synchronized cooking that finishes both together. For a family that wants sticky rice and a protein from one machine, that saves a pot.

The tray adds steps and cleaning, and the control is less specialized for glutinous rice than the CUCKOO's dedicated mode. You will set water and soak time yourself. Compared with the Zojirushi it is less precise, but the tray is a real convenience.

Wash the tray and inner pot after each use. Starchy rice sticks to the pot, so soak it with warm water straight away. It suits cooks who value a one-pot meal more than perfect control. Rinse the tray promptly, since sticky starch bakes onto it if left overnight.
products.bestFor: Families who want rice and a side cooked together.
pros: Tacook tray cooks a dish above the rice

products.name: BLACK+DECKER RC516 16-Cup Rice Cooker with Steaming Basket
products.description:
The RC516 is a simple one-touch cooker with a big pot. It cooks up to 8 cups of uncooked rice, yielding up to 16 cups, and includes a steaming basket and a removable nonstick bowl. For sticky rice for a crowd, the capacity is the draw.

The tradeoff is control. A one-touch cooker has no fuzzy logic, so glutinous rice has to be managed by soaking and careful water measurement, and a thick, sticky batch can scorch at the bottom. Compared with the Zojirushi it is a basic heater with a thermostat, but it costs much less and feeds many more people.

Soak the rice, use the minimum water and avoid opening the lid early. Wash the bowl soon after use. It suits large households and gatherings where capacity matters more than precision. Its size also makes it a sensible pick for potlucks and holiday meals.
products.bestFor: Large gatherings that need up to 8 cups of uncooked rice.
cons: One-touch control with no fuzzy logic

products.name: TOSHIBA Small Rice Cooker 3 Cup with LCD and 8 Functions
products.description:
The Toshiba is a small smart cooker with an LCD display and eight functions that include white rice, quick cook and brown rice. Moisture sensing adjusts temperature and time as it cooks, which helps with sticky grains that behave differently from batch to batch.

The compromise is size and a lack of a dedicated glutinous setting in the specs. Three cups uncooked suits one to three people. Compared with the CUCKOO CR-0375FG it has a clearer display but no explicit sticky rice menu.

Use the white rice program with a reduced water amount and a long soak. Wash the pot promptly. It suits singles and couples who want a modern display in a small cooker. Use the quick cook mode sparingly, because sticky rice benefits from the slower standard cycle.
products.bestFor: One to three people who want a small cooker with a clear display.

products.name: Aroma ARC-363-1NGB 3 Cup Uncooked Rice Cooker and Steamer
products.description:
The Aroma ARC-363-1NGB is a basic one-touch cooker with a steam tray, listed for two to six cups. It handles rice, soups and steamed vegetables, and the one-touch operation means you press and walk away. At a low outlay, it is the simplest way to cook sticky rice in a standard cooker.

As a thermostat cooker it has no fuzzy logic and no sticky rice setting. The pot can scorch if the water is too low, and the result depends on your soak and ratio. Compared with the Tiger, it has a steam tray but not synchronized cooking.

Soak the rice well, use the minimum water and wash the pot at once. It suits budget buyers who will tune the method. Do not skip the soak just because the lid closes with one touch.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want a simple cooker with a steam tray.

products.name: AROMA Digital Rice Cooker 4 Cup Uncooked with Steam Tray
products.description:
The AROMA Digital cooker has programmable digital controls with presets for white rice, brown rice, steam and flash rice, plus an automatic keep-warm mode. It also includes a steam tray so you can cook above the rice. For sticky rice, the digital timer helps with repeatable results.

The tradeoff is that it lacks fuzzy logic and a sticky rice preset. You still manage the soak and the water. Compared with the 3 cup Aroma it holds a cup more and has a better control panel, and compared with the CUCKOO it is less specialized.

Keep the steam vent and lid clean and avoid long keep-warm periods, since sticky rice dries out. It suits cooks who want programmable controls at a modest price. Avoid leaving rice on keep-warm for many hours, since glutinous rice dries and hardens.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want programmable controls at a modest price.
pros: Presets including steam and flash rice
cons: Sticky rice dries on long keep-warm

buyingCriteria.explanation: Glutinous rice cooks best after a soak of several hours, and with much less water than regular rice, often close to a 1 to 1 ratio. A cooker that lets you set a manual water level and does not add its own soak is more predictable. Fuzzy logic models like the Zojirushi and CUCKOO adjust heat for you, while basic models like the Aroma depend on your method. Rinse the rice only until the water is mostly clear, since over-rinsing can make glutinous rice mushy.

The CUCKOO CR-0375FG lists a glutinous white rice option, and the Zojirushi offers multiple menu selections. A dedicated menu changes the soak time and the heat curve, which matters because sticky rice scorches. Without one, use the white rice setting with reduced water, and expect to experiment. If your cooker has none, reduce the water a little each time and keep notes until the texture is right.

Sticky rice sits densely and holds heat, so a hot spot burns the bottom layer. The Zojirushi's spherical pan promotes uniform heating, and fuzzy logic cooks adjust the heat curve. A basic thermostat cooker like the BLACK+DECKER RC516 switches only when the pot gets hot, so it is more likely to leave a crust. Resting the cooked rice with the lid on for ten minutes lets steam redistribute and loosens the bottom layer.

A 3 cup uncooked cooker like the CUCKOO or Toshiba makes six cups cooked. A 5.5 cup cooker like the Zojirushi or Tiger feeds a family. The BLACK+DECKER RC516 manages up to 8 cups. Sticky rice expands less than regular rice, so use cooked weight as a guide and avoid overfilling. Filling a cooker to the top is a mistake, because starch foam can climb out of the vent.

Traditional sticky rice is steamed, not boiled. Cookers with steam trays, such as the Aroma models and the BLACK+DECKER, let you steam soaked rice above boiling water for a closer result. Cooking it directly in the pot gives a denser, stickier result. Decide which texture you prefer. A cheesecloth under the rice makes lifting and cleaning much easier in a tray.

Sticky rice leaves a thick layer on the pot and lid. Removable nonstick bowls and a self-clean function, as on the CUCKOO, make cleanup easier. Soak the pot immediately after serving, because dried starch is hard to remove. A nonstick pot needs a soft paddle to avoid scratching. A pot with a worn coating sticks much worse, which is the first sign it is time to replace it.

faq.q: Can a rice cooker make good sticky rice?
faq.a: Yes, with a soak and less water. Fuzzy logic cookers like the Zojirushi and CUCKOO give more consistent results than basic thermostats. Expect to adjust the water by a few tablespoons over the first few batches.

faq.q: How long should I soak glutinous rice?
faq.a: Several hours, often four or more, improves texture. A shorter soak works but gives a firmer grain.

faq.q: How much water do I use?
faq.a: Much less than regular rice, often close to 1 to 1. Check your cooker's manual and adjust by small amounts.
Traditional sticky rice is steamed for a lighter, chewier result. Cooking it in the pot gives a denser texture.
Dense rice and high heat. Use less water, a fuzzy logic cooker or a lower heat setting. A pot with a worn coating also scorches more easily.

faq.q: Can I use the same cooker for white rice?
faq.a: Yes. All of these cook regular rice. Clean the pot well between batches.
